title: The uncle's rules
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The uncle has rules for the shack. They're painted on a board. Gully knows them by heart. Wood reads them and finds the fourth one is about him.

panels.composition: Inside the shack. A board on the wall, hand-painted, five lines of rules drawn as blocks. GULLY coiling rope. WOOD reading the board.

image.prompt: the inside of a shingle bait shack with a hand-painted board of rules on the wall, a teenager coiling rope, a young man reading the board, black and white, no words
image.notes: The rules as blocks; only rule four legible. Letter after: '4. NO DRAWING ON THE COUNTER.'

panels.composition: Rule four, legible: NO DRAWING ON THE COUNTER. Older than Wood. The paint cracked.

image.prompt: close on a cracked hand-painted rule on a wooden board, black and white, no words
a young man pointing at a painted board while a teenager coils rope without looking, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The counter's edge, worn. Under the varnish, faint: a gull. Two strokes. Not Wood's. Somebody's, 1978.

image.prompt: close on a worn wooden counter edge with a faint two-stroke bird scratched under old varnish, black and white, no words
image.notes: A gull under the varnish, 1978. Reserved who.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Rule four is older than him. The gull under the varnish: reserved.
